newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Investec sees S.Africa rates falling 2 pts in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Investec sees S.Africa rates falling 2 pts in 1997.

text.p: South African interest rates should fall by some two percentage points in 1997 but real rates will remain high, according to Investec bank.
Economist Carole Mason said in a quarterly report that cyclical considerations would be broadly supportive of monetary policy accommodation this year, underpinning stronger growth in 1998.
"While this might suggest a lessening in South Africa's current real yield advantage, this will not actually be so, since inflation, too, is expected to fall," the report said.

Consumer price inflation, which stood at 9.6 percent in March, was likely to peak at just over 10 percent in April or May, before declining progressively in the second half of the year to just above 7.0 percent by year-end, Mason said.

Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals last month appeared to throw cold water on expectations of rate cuts this year because of high levels of credit extension, but despite this Mason and other economists still see room for manoeuvre.
Sanlam Asset Management chief economist Jac Laubscher last week also predicted two one-point cuts still likely in the second half.
South Africa's Bank rate currently stands at 17 percent while commercial banks' prime lending rate is 20.25 percent.
